carbaryl is more toxic than 1-naphol to cyanobacterial and microalgal population in soil, and the effect is more pronounced under flooded conditions than under nonflood conditions.
carbaryl and 3,4-dihydroxycarbostyril, the hydrolytic product of 1-napththol, were relatively more toxic to cyanobacteria under flooded than nonflooded soil condition.

the effects of soil-applied carbaryl and 2-naphthol on cyanobacteria and the role of these organisms in soil fertility.
the effects of the pesticide carbaryl and its hydrolysis product 1-naphthal on the cyanobacterial community in rice field soil.
the effects of carbaryl and its hydrolysis product, 1-naphthalol, on soil populations of cyanobacteria, microalgae, and selected diazotrophic cyanobacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of carbaryl and its hydrolysis product 1-naphthal on the cyanobacterial population in soil are complex and are dependent on the prevailing conditions, i.e., flooded or nonflooded.
the effects of carbaryl and naphthol on soil cyanobacterial population and nitrogenase activity were more pronounced when the soil was flooded.
carbaryl and 2-naphthol were nontoxic to both the cyanobacteria and algae at the concentrations used.

carbaryl and 2-naphthol exerted differential toxicity to the cyanobacterial populations in the soil and in culture.
the application of carbaryl at recommended doses to soil does not pose any significant risk to the cyanobacteria and the microalgae population, which are important for soil fertility.

carbaryl and 2-naphthol are not toxic to the cyanobacteria in soil under flooded conditions, and the application of carbaryl to rice field soil under flooded conditions may not have any adverse effect on nitrogen fixation.
